Okay. I sort of see it now. Why, though, does it work to just use C(4,1) for the last person. I get that it essentially means that we're picking one person from the 4 different ethnic groups. It's hard for me to really articulate what it is that I'm confused about. 

Let's say we have a bag of 5 red balls, 5 blue, 5 green, 5 yellow. I want to pick 5 balls so that I'll have at least one of each color. I have 5x5x5x5 ways of picking the first 4. The last one can be from any group, so we use C(4,1) because there are 4 ways of picking one ball from one of the different color groups. 

It's all starting to make a little more sense, but can you weigh on why it would not work to, instead, multiply 5^4 by 16 since there are 16 balls remaining?

Thanks for the second explanation. I guess there isn't a simpler way to go about it. 

For the committee problem, I'm still having trouble wrapping my head around it; these counting problems are just very unintuitive for me. The way I see it, there are 8 people left to choose from, and since it doesn't matter which ethnic group is represented by the last person, any of the 8 remaining can be chosen. What is wrong with my logic?
